MA Wahhab Miah, Advocate  --- For the Petitioners.

parties:
Fisheries Research Institute and others ------ Petitioner
Vs.
MR Bhuyain Ltd and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment: 10. As against this Mr Md Rafiqul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate, for the plaintiff opposite party, submits that in the present case when the award has not been made Rule of the court it becomes a dead horse and as it is a dead horse a suit on the original cause of section can be maintained. In support of his submission he relied on the case of Ram Shar vs Babu Lal, reported in AIR 1965 (Allahabad) 217 wherein it has been held that if an award has not been made a Rule of court it remains a dead letter. A suit on the original cause of action is maintainable and it cannot be successfully resisted by setting up such award in defence. The same view has been expressed in the case of Sait Pamandass Sugharam vs TS Manikyam Pillai and others reported in AIR 1960 (Andhra Pro) 59. Mr Md Rafiqul Islam Bhuiyan also placed reliance in the case of both Pamandas Sugharam (died) by Hardevi and others vs TS Manikyam Pillai and another, reported in AIR 1963 (Andhra Pra) 28, where it has been held that where an award has not been acted upon and the defendant has not taken steps to have the award filed and gone through the formalities enjoined by the specific provisions of the Arbitration Act, it is not open to him to set up the award as bar to an action that may be brought against him and it is not open to the court to dismiss a suit on the basis of an award which has not been filed into court and in respect of which a decree has not been passed. Mr Bhuiyan also submits that when an award has not been made Rule of the Court, this cannot stand in the way of getting the decree by the plaintiff in a properly framed suit on the previous cause of action and in support of this he placed reliance in the case of Wali Mohammad and others vs Pano and others, reported in ATR 1960 (Patna) 128, where it has been held that an award given on reference without the intervention of the court has no legal existence nor is it capable of upholding any right or title as comprehended thereunder unless it is made a Rule of the court within the meaning of the Arbitration Act. He submits that in the present case the award that has been given has not been made Rule of the court and as such there is no bar in filing of the present suit. The same view has been expressed in the case of Habiba Khatoon and others vs Nawab Lal reported in AIR 1961 (Patna) 372. He also submitted that sections 31-32 and 33 the Arbitration Act has not by express language or by implication, provided that a suit on the original cause of action after an abortive or incomplete arbitration would not lie and Mr Bhuiyan placed reliance in the case of Chandraghago Sadashj and another vs Bhakachand Mansaji, reported in AIR 1959 (Born) 549, where it has been held that the scheme of the Arbitration Act appears to be to bring all arbitrations under the control of the court and treat them as effective only if a decree was obtained on the award in accordance with the Act and to prevent the parties from agitating any question relating to existence of validity or effect of an arbitration agreement or award in any manner other than that provided by the Act. It has also been held that sections 31, 32 and 33 do not by express language or by implication provide that a suit on the original cause of action after an abortive or incomplete arbitration would not lie. Mr Bhuiyan also placed reliance in the case of the Provine of West Pakistan vs Mustafa RGC Pipe Works Karachi reported in PLD 1977 (Karachi) 397, where it has been held that award not filed in court does not bar filing of Civil suit unless acted upon.
